title: [YouPass Collect] - Cinema visits in Australia from 1996 to 2000

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table and line graph illustrate cinema attendance rates and the average number of visits among Australians, along with a breakdown by four age groups, from 1996 to 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the percentage of the population going to the cinema rose and then remained steady, the average number of visits fell after 1997. Across all age groups, a similar up-and-down pattern was seen, with the 14-24 group consistently going to the cinema the most and the over-50s the least.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: In 1996, 62% of Australians went to the cinema, with each person visiting an average of 10.3 times. Both figures increased the following year, to 72% and 11.1 visits, respectively. From 1998 onwards, however, attendance stayed stable at between 70% and 72%, while the average number of visits dropped to 8.3 and remained at roughly this level until 2000.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the age-group data, in 1996, the 14-24 group recorded 15 visits, followed by the 25-35 and 35-49 groups at 14 and 12, respectively, while the over-50s had the fewest at 10. All four groups rose and fell together, reaching highs in 1997 and 1999 and lows in 1998 and 2000. For instance, the youngest group climbed to 22 in 1997, dropped to 16 in 1998, peaked at 23 in 1999, then fell back to 18 in 2000. The other three groups followed the same pattern, with the 25-35, 35-49, and over-50 groups finishing the period at 17, 15, and 13 visits, respectively.
